replaced: 23 October 2026, owner: the GameCube emulator is OUR OWN, written from scratch like cBoy and the arcade core, not Dolphin and not a wrapper (own cores exist to get rid of credits and outside licences). This Dolphin plan is not to be followed.
title: GameCube and Wii on Dolphin, made fast without JIT by an interpreter of our own (owner, 16 October 2026)
why: On 16 October the owner played Star Wars Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader on Manic EMU on their iPhone 17 Pro Max with no JIT, on Dolphin's Cached Interpreter, nearly flawlessly. GameCube had been wrongly called impossible without JIT (docs/HARD_SYSTEMS.md, corrected). Manic's core is libretro Dolphin (github.com/Daiuno/dolphin, a fork of libretro/dolphin, GPL-2.0-or-later) with its own faster interpreter on the manicInterpreter branch. The owner: 'I want to do what Manic did to Dolphin.' So: Dolphin (open licence, no limits on the app) as the GameCube and Wii emulator, plus a faster interpreter that is OUR OWN CODE, written by us from how the CPU core works, never copied from Manic's branch (the owner wants to build away from other people's code). Dolphin's credit goes in the folded Open-source credits list (OpenSourceCreditsList in native/ios/SettingsScreen.swift); its source link must point at our pinned upstream plus our patches.
facts: Source: github.com/libretro/dolphin (Dolphin with a libretro front end in Source/Core/DolphinLibretro, merged with upstream Dolphin on 7 August 2026 and active daily; Vulkan glue in DolphinLibretro/Vulkan.cpp; 'libretro: build fixes for iOS/tvOS' 3fa2bdae6). Licence GPL-2.0-or-later, fine inside Continuum's GPL-3.0.

CPU cores in Dolphin: Interpreter, Cached Interpreter, JIT (JitArm64 on the phone). Without JIT only the two interpreters may run; anything that writes and runs machine code is killed by iOS. The engine's JIT gate is crates/emulator-bridge/src/jit.rs (core_may_use_jit, GET_JIT_CAPABLE, the jit26 region on TXM phones).

What Manic changed (read 16 October, for the ideas only): blocks dispatched as a chain of guaranteed tail calls, blocks linked so the chain runs past a block boundary, hot instructions with their own callbacks, pairs of common integer and memory instructions fused into one callback, op bodies inlined from headers, RAM accesses resolved inline, each BAT page resolved to a host pointer once, LR and CTR split out of the SPR handlers. Same behaviour as the Cached Interpreter. Ours must be written by us and proved identical to the Cached Interpreter.
Dolphin release 2603 sped up MMU emulation a lot; libretro/dolphin has it since its August merge.

Video on the phone: Dolphin's Vulkan backend through the engine's Vulkan hardware path (MoltenVK on wgpu's own MTLDevice, the finished image adopted as a Metal texture with no copy: gfx/vulkan_hw.rs, gfx/moltenvk_device.rs), proven with Beetle PSX HW, PPSSPP and Azahar. This sandbox has no GPU and no Vulkan, so host proofs use Dolphin's Null or Software video backend.

detect.rs already recognises GameCube and Wii discs by their magic words; ImportCenter.swift and ContinuumApp.swift currently list them as systems this build can't run. Dolphin needs its Sys folder (game settings database and more) in the system directory: bundle it like prboom.wad / the players.

The owner's phone has no JIT (iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 26, TXM). JIT stays required for everyone who can enable it (owner-rules): Dolphin's ARM64 JIT on non-TXM debugged phones and through the jit26 region, like the PPSSPP and Azahar patches.
hard_rules: Nothing of Manic's goes in: not its code, not its interpreter's name, not its option wording. Our CPU core gets its own name and is designed from our own profiling of where Dolphin's Cached Interpreter spends its time on the host. Credits name Dolphin and its authors only (owner-rules, 'Do what Manic does, never the way Manic looks').

Dolphin is an OPTIONAL core (IOS_OPTIONAL_CORES, its own recipe region in scripts/build-core.sh): if it fails to compile, the .ipa ships without it and GameCube games say so in one plain line. Only its own fingerprint may change (prove with ios-fingerprint on two other cores), and run scripts/check-core-cache.sh.
Never let Dolphin pick the JIT unless jit::core_may_use_jit says yes; the default CPU core is the fastest interpreter.

Our interpreter is our own code (comments naming the PowerPC behaviour), in scripts/patches/dolphin-*.patch, never Manic's code. Prove it gives exactly the Cached Interpreter's results (CPU state compared block by block on the same programs) before it is offered, and measure its speed against the Cached Interpreter.
Never fetch or commit a commercial game, BIOS (IPL) or Wii keys. Test with open-licence homebrew and our own programs only.
Every commit ends with [skip ci]. No branches, no PRs, never edit .github/workflows/, STATUS.md, TESTING.md or HANDOFF.md. Anything a player reads is short, casual and plain.

items.title: Dolphin in the app, GameCube and Wii playable on the Cached Interpreter
items.detail: Pin libretro/dolphin, add its recipe region (CMake iOS build as a libretro dylib, Vulkan backend on, JIT code compiled but off, no Qt), the Sys folder bundled, core options rules (CPU core forced to an interpreter unless JIT is allowed; sensible phone defaults like 1x internal resolution and shader compilation that doesn't stutter), the GameCube and Wii systems and extensions routed to it (remove them from the can't-run lists), a CoreSpec, the GameCube touch pad (A, B, X, Y, Z, L, R, Start, stick, C-stick) and a basic Wii layout, memory cards and save states, the credits row, core_updates.rs (a new pinned core: the tests may need a rule for cores new in this install). Prove on the host: build the core for Linux, boot open-licence GameCube homebrew through the engine with the Null or Software backend, save state round-trip, measure Cached Interpreter speed.

items.title: Our own faster interpreter (Continuum's CPU core for GameCube and Wii)
items.detail: A new CPU core in Dolphin, written by us: chained blocks through guaranteed tail calls ([[clang::musttail]]), linked blocks, fast paths for hot instructions, fused instruction pairs, inline RAM access, per-page host pointers. Proof: identical CPU state to the Cached Interpreter after every block over long runs of several programs, plus Dolphin's own CPU tests where available; speed measured against the Cached Interpreter on the host. Then make it the default, keep the Cached Interpreter as a per-game choice ('CPU' in the game's core settings), as Manic does.

items.title: JIT when the phone allows it
items.detail: Dolphin's ARM64 JIT for players who can switch JIT on, through the engine's existing gate and the jit26 region on TXM phones, the way the PPSSPP and Azahar patches do it. Never required; untestable on the owner's phone.

items.title: Wii controls
items.detail: Wii Remote (pointer from touch, shake from the motion sensor), Nunchuk and Classic Controller choices per game, the sensor-bar pointer, Wii saves; touch layouts for each.

items.title: Write it up
